judge_verdict.summary: The agent emailed the detective but then contacted the wrong lawyer, skipped the required detective-reply condition, and sent too many user messages, so the verifier FAIL is correct.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct. The timed GAIA2 verifier runs in action mode and awards pass only when write-action counts match the oracle within tolerance and each action semantically matches; any tool-count mismatch zeroes the reward [3][5]. The verifier reported binary_reward 0 with reward 0.0 [1]. The user task required waiting one minute, emailing the detective if more than five John Smith emails arrive, notifying the user when that detective email is sent, then waiting two minutes for a detective reply that provides a lawyer contact before emailing that lawyer and forwarding the harassment emails [2]. The reference oracle emails Caoimhe, sends the exact message "The email to the detective has been sent.", then—after a detective-reply environment event—emails sergei.petrov@moscowlawyers.ru and forwards six John Smith emails to him [4]. The agent called are_get_time and immediately listed inbox emails without any 60-second wait_for_notification [6], did email the detective and notify the user, but used different wording than the oracle message [7], then during its 120-second wait received a notification from lea.mueller-schulze@gaia2mail.com rather than a reply from the detective [8]. It nevertheless emailed lea.muller-schulze-lawyer@gaia2mail.com and forwarded the six harassment emails to her instead of sergei.petrov@moscowlawyers.ru, violating the conditional requirement that the lawyer contact come from the detective's reply [4][9]. It also issued three AgentUserInterface__send_message_to_user calls, exceeding the oracle's one plus the single allowed extra [10]. The agent accomplished the detective-email portion of the workflow but did not truly complete the timed harassment-escalation task as specified, so TN is the right classification.

evidence.claim: The verifier reported FAIL with binary_reward 0 and continuous reward 0.0.

The user task is a conditional timed workflow: wait one minute, check for more than five John Smith emails, email the detective and notify the user, wait two minutes for a detective reply that gives a lawyer contact, then email that lawyer and forward the one-minute John Smith emails.

citations.quote: An individual named John Smith keeps harassing me. Wait exactly 1 minute and check if I receive more than 5 emails from him (his email is johnsmith@gaia2mail.com) and if so, look for my detective contact and email them right away letting them know what is happening, asking if they know a good lawyer in Moscow and for safety advice. Let me know when the email to the detective was sent. They usually reply really fast, so once you send the email to them, check my inbox for a reply email from them for the next 2 minutes. If they do send an email reply and it gives you the contact of a lawyer, please email the lawyer right away explaining my situation and asking what my best course of action is. Then, forward them all the emails I received in that one minute from John Smith.

evidence.claim: This task uses GAIA2 time config, which grades agent write actions against oracle_events.json in action mode.

The reference solution emails the detective, sends the exact user message "The email to the detective has been sent.", then emails sergei.petrov@moscowlawyers.ru and forwards six harassment emails to him after a detective-reply environment event.
In action mode the verifier requires matching write-tool counts within tolerance; a mismatch forces reward 0.0 regardless of partial action matches.

matched_fraction = len(matched_oracle_indices) / len(oracle_actions)
    reward = matched_fraction if counts_match else 0.0
